title: Willis Young presses Lester to improve his reading
summary: Phillips denies Lester was thrown out of the family band; the father told him to read properly and get a proper clarinet, and had the clout to supply good horns.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: One question about the reading. Lester had trouble with his father one time, when his father wanted him to improve on his reading.
Do you remember that? I understood that he got kicked out of the band until he could learn to read better.
No. How he gonna kick him out, man?
I don't know. You tell me. You tell the story.

I'm just saying, if he kick him out, that was the band! Ha-ha. You know what I mean. That's what people were looking at. They weren't thinking about his reading. They were thinking about them solos he played.
Well, is it true that Willis Young got on him for...

Oh yeah. He told him one time, 'Lester, you got to get up on your reading. You ain't reading quite...' I thought he was. Because the way he played it to me, he was fakin' it, but it sounded good to us. But he wasn't playing it like it's supposed to be, he said. He said, 'Another thing, I want you to get rid of that damn clarinet and get you a clarinet, and I'm going to take...' He got them. See, his father had this influence in Minneapolis. He could go anywhere and get anything he wanted. I played all kind of trumpets -- Conns, he'd bring me and ask me how I liked that one. Conns, Kings. Bueshers. So I finally wound up, he gave me a Buesher. He gave it to me for Christmas. He gave me a Buesher for trumpet; pretty one, too. I swapped it off for... I met a boy, a young guy up in Jamestown, North Dakota, and...
